title: How work
lede: Balance bugs, critical features and nice-to-haves, with feedback loops running through all of it.

items.title: Major bugs
items.text: Anything that disrupts how people use the site. Fixed first, before anything merges.

items.title: Critical features
items.text: What the site needs to do what people come to do: search, map, profiles, connect.

items.title: Minor bugs and easy fixes
items.text: Picked up when a dev has spare hours in the sprint.

items.title: Nice-to-haves
items.text: Logged in the backlog. Never displace P0–P1.

items.title: Kickoff · Day 1 (Monday)
items.text: Dev leads break down the sprint theme, read everyone's hours from the contributor sheet, and assign one feature per dev or mob, sized to fit two weeks.

items.title: Mobs form
items.text: Small teams of 3–5 per feature. Each mob opens a branch and a draft PR on day one, which gives it a preview link straight away.

items.title: Updates · daily or weekly
items.text: Async in Discord: shipped / next / blocked, plus a screenshot or clip. Weekly minimum, daily when a mob is active.

items.title: Mid-sprint check · Day 7
items.text: Anything at risk? Cut scope early. Re-shuffle bug fixes to whoever has hours.

items.title: Demo + retro · Day 14
items.text: Each mob shows what works on its preview link. Keep / change in the process.

items.title: Monthly review call
items.text: The Project Director and dev leads approve, reject or send back the month's work. Only approved work is pushed to main.
Works on desktop and mobile, on a Vercel preview link.
PR reviewed by someone outside the mob, with a short step-by-step review list (HUMAN_REVIEW.md style).
No new P0s; lint and checks pass.
Tagged frontend / backend; board and HQ updated.
Before/after screenshot or clip posted in the update.
Approved at the review call before it lands on main.
